key_insight: A reproducible six-site RNA splicing signature can accurately distinguish ReNU syndrome caused by RNU4-2 T-loop variants from controls and may serve as a quantitative biomarker for therapy development.
clinical_relevance: This cross-tissue biomarker could help stratify patients, track disease severity, and support preclinical and clinical testing of future treatments for ReNU syndrome.
method: Compared RNA-sequencing from two independent cohorts of people with ReNU syndrome and controls.
Focused on shared alternative splicing events, especially alternative 5' splice-site (A5SS) changes.
Derived a minimal six-site signature and tested it across blood controls and an iPSC-to-neuron model.
evidence_signal: Across 30 individuals with ReNU syndrome and 54 controls, the six-site signature perfectly separated 19 n.64_65insT cases from controls and showed no false positives in 5,984 additional whole-blood controls.
watch_item: The signature appears specific to T-loop variants and may not generalize equally well to Stem III variants or all tissue contexts without further validation.
paper_title: A cross-tissue splicing signature as a quantitative biomarker for ReNU syndrome
